note: Real-ELF ProgramTest for the canonical Rational Representation V2 waist -- open-market structured issuance/unwrap/denominate/reconstitute plus terminal redemption (blocked.json: 'A real-ELF ProgramTest for this route already exists and passes; it simply does not emit census evidence yet'). Real Claims, Custody, Registry and Core ELFs plus the genuine, canonically-built Token-2022 v11 runtime, with the Product graph and LiabilityBasisV2 aggregate INSTALLED directly. Campaign: programs/dclutch-claims-sbf/tests/rational_representation_v2_program_test.rs. Every submitted transaction goes through a test-only wrapper that CPIs into Claims, so a refusal Claims itself raises propagates the same numeric code to the wrapper's own top-level failure log -- a failed CPI aborts the whole transaction before the wrapper's Rust code regains control, so that repetition is the runtime's own account of the failure depth, not a second refusal.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: create the Claims-role Custody replay
bindings.note: The Claims-role Custody replay this Market's redemption needs, CREATED rather than planted. Claims forwards a Custody InitializeReplay under its own release-pinned caller authority; Custody creates the account at the role-seeded replay PDA (decision 0008 section 7). Every terminal case in this campaign now opens with this transaction, so the redemption below consumes the cursor the chain actually wrote -- revision 1, zero open Vaults -- instead of one the fixture invented. 711 legacy bytes against the 1,232 limit, asserted: creating this cursor must not require a published lookup table.

bindings.note: Creation is permissionless, so the second submitter has to lose HARMLESSLY. Claims requires the replay account to be vacant and System-owned before it forwards anything, so this refuses Identity (0x5002) before Custody is reached; the campaign asserts the live cursor is byte-identical and the first prepayer keeps the rent refund.

The winning terminal redemption refuses Identity (0x5002) and the campaign asserts the Hoard and the recipient are byte-identical. Custody would refuse it a layer down on ReplayBindingMismatch; the point is that Claims does not get there.

bindings.note: HOSTILE. A same-width RepresentationDescriptorV2 whose coefficients are the canonical ones PERMUTED -- a valid record naming a recipe the composition does not state. Built by mutating the DERIVED preimage, so it is a near-miss of the real record rather than a hand-written seventh one. Refused twice for two reasons: host-side, require_coefficients_are_the_composition_root will not mint it (the join the live route lost when authenticate_exposure replaced authenticate_graph, decision 0011 s3d); on chain, Identity (0x5002) because the request names a descriptor_id that is the digest of other bytes.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: receipt backed by receipt
bindings.note: HOSTILE, and the campaign records WHERE it dies rather than claiming Claims caught it. Coordinate zero's asset row and account frame name the RECEIPT Mint, so a receipt would be backed by itself. RepresentationRequestV2::decode refuses those bytes outright (AccountAlias), and EVERY caller must decode the request to derive its own Trading authority (CallerAuthoritySeedsV1 over the request's parent_context) -- so the request can never acquire a signer and never reaches the Claims CPI at all. The test-only wrapper refuses at its own Instruction code (0x104000) at 11,302 CU. The founding-time half is proved separately in the same test: StructuredTermsV2::bind_shard_terms refuses a receipt Mint aliasing a shard Mint with DuplicateIdentity.

unnamed_refusal.reason: RationalV2CallerError::Instruction, raised by the campaign's TEST-ONLY wrapper program, not by a first-party dClutch program. That is the honest depth: the wrapper decodes the request to derive its Trading caller authority exactly as a real caller must, so a request the grammar rejects can never acquire a signer and can never reach the Claims CPI. Recorded as unnamed because the wrapper's refusal band is test scaffolding and must not enter any program's taxonomy.

The callee recomputes K_i = S * c_i as asset.coefficient * header.quantity (plan.rs:263) and the campaign basis [2, 3, 5] over 7 is pairwise coprime and coprime to the denominator precisely so a one-atom skew at one coordinate cannot be presented as a legitimate quantity at another. bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: issue against a receipt Mint with only the Mint role
bindings.note: HOSTILE, and it CORRECTS decision 0011 s3b. The receipt Mint carries the representation authority as its Mint authority and NOT as its permissioned-burn authority: s3b's under-configured founding, which the ruling predicted would let Issue commit and then fail at BurnReceipt 'at the Token program with the descriptor already committed'. Measured: parse_behavior_mint reads the receipt Mint's Token-2022 behavior profile on every action and requires the permissioned-burn authority present and pinned, so the FIRST IssueStructured refuses Token (0x5009) at 255,972 CU with ZERO Token-2022 CPIs issued. The two-role cost is real; its consequence is a founding that can never issue, not a representation that can never be unwound.

bindings.label: claims rational-representation-v2: unwrap against a receipt Mint with only the Mint role
bindings.note: The consequence of the row above, recorded for what it is rather than for what it looks like: the Issue committed nothing, so no representation replay exists to carry revision one and the unwrap is refused on Accounts (0x5001) at 251,184 CU. BurnReceipt is never the thing that fails, because there is never anything to unwrap.
